Internal helper: the code and the label behind each category of a factor

Source: R/classify.R
dot-jst_level_codes.Rd

An analysis turns a grouping or crosstab variable into a factor of its categories, and stores what it printed: the factor's levels, or each category formatted under the call's value.id mode. Neither is the category's code. This reads the code off the cells: for each level, the value the variable holds in the first case of that category – a labelled variable's code, a numeric variable's number, a text variable's text (its blank cells the one <blank> category) – and the level itself for a factor, whose levels are its categories, and for any other type (a date, TRUE/FALSE), whose printed level is its value. The label is the value label of that code, whole, or NA (.jst_value_label_of()). Read off the cells, so it needs no agreement between the factor's level order and a separately sorted list of codes. Session 399 (Capability Slate T's build 0).

Usage

.jst_level_codes(f, src, val_labels = NULL)

Arguments

f

The factor the analysis made, every level held by a case (after droplevels()).

src

The variable the factor was made from, case for case: the same length and order.

val_labels

The variable's value labels, or NULL.

Value

A data frame, one row per level in level order: level, code (numeric or character), label (character).
